forces.title: Ambitious Government Targets for PNG and CNG Expansion
forces.description: The Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB) has set ambitious targets for City Gas Distribution (CGD), aiming for 126.3 million PNG connections and 18,336 CNG stations by 2034. State-level policies are driving a 25% rise in CNG vehicles and over 2.1 million new PNG connections in 2024-25. These concrete goals provide a strong policy push and clear growth trajectory for the sector, indicating sustained expansion in infrastructure and customer base.

forces.title: Growing Demand from Residential and Transport Sectors
forces.description: India's natural gas consumption is driven by various sectors, with residential and transport being key end-customers for CGD. Rapid urbanisation, increasing household incomes, and escalating industrial activities contribute to consistently growing demand. Specifically, increased adoption of CNG-powered vehicles, coupled with an expanding network of CNG stations (from 1,730 in 2019 to 7,444 by 9MFY25), fuels significant volume growth for CGD, where CNG accounts for 60% of consumption.

forces.title: Underperformance Against PNG Connection Targets
forces.description: Despite ambitious targets set by PNGRB for 12.6 crore PNG (Domestic) connections by 2032, actual connections reached only 1.4 crore as of February 28, 2025, significantly behind the target of 2.9 crore connections for that period. This underperformance indicates potential challenges in infrastructure rollout, customer adoption, or other operational hurdles, posing a headwind to the sector's rapid expansion plans for household gas distribution.

forces.title: LPG Consumer Base Saturation Driving PNG Adoption
forces.description: The LPG consumer base is nearing saturation due to significant penetration, with expected annual growth of only 1-2% going forward. Concurrently, the government is increasing its focus on promoting PNG (Domestic) usage. This trend, coupled with potential LPG under-recoveries or price increases, suggests that PNG is well-positioned to gradually replace LPG demand, particularly among non-PMUY users, acting as a significant tailwind for CGD's market penetration and volume growth.

forces.title: Support for Compressed Biogas (CBG) in CGD Network
forces.description: The Union Budget 2024-25 allocated Rs. 497.25 crore (US$ 59.75 million) to a scheme dedicated to developing pipeline infrastructure for injecting Compressed Biogas (CBG) into City Gas Distribution (CGD) networks. This financial support promotes diversification of gas sources within CGD, enhancing supply reliability and potentially reducing dependence on traditional natural gas, while aligning with cleaner fuel objectives.

viewpoints.title: CGD sector vital for India's natural gas consumption growth and energy mix target
viewpoints.description: CareEdge Ratings emphasizes the crucial role of the Indian City Gas Distribution (CGD) sector in achieving the national goal of elevating natural gas's share to 15% in the primary energy mix by 2030, up from 6.5% (as of 2024). The CGD industry is key for efficient last-mile connectivity, bridging the gap between national gas networks and end consumers. This strategic importance highlights a positive outlook for the sector's expansion and sustained growth.

viewpoints.title: Positive outlook for CGD revenue growth, supported by volume and coverage expansion
viewpoints.description: CareEdge Ratings projects a positive revenue outlook for key CGD industry players, anticipating a Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR) of 18% from FY25 to FY27. This growth is primarily driven by the expansion of CGD coverage and increasing gas consumption volumes. Despite potential near-term compression in debt coverage metrics due to significant capital expenditures, the financial profiles of these companies are expected to remain comfortable, supported by their modular capex approach and sponsor financial strength.

demand_drivers.driver: Government Initiative to Elevate Natural Gas Share
demand_drivers.description: The Government of India aims to increase natural gas's contribution to 15% of the energy mix by 2030, up from 6.5% in 2024, driving demand for CGD services.
These factors contribute to a consistent increase in the demand for natural gas, particularly in household and commercial segments served by CGD.
Industrial consumers are a significant portion of natural gas demand, driving consumption for CGD networks.

market_sizing.methodology: Forecasted growth in the share of natural gas in India's primary energy mix, indicating the potential market expansion for gas distribution.

demand_drivers.description: Increased reach and connectivity of city gas distribution infrastructure will naturally expand its share of total natural gas consumption.
Growth in CNG vehicles and PNG domestic connections will boost CGD's consumption share.

market_sizing.methodology: CGD's forecasted contribution to India's overall natural gas consumption. This represents the market share of the CGD sector within the broader natural gas market.

demand_drivers.description: Three-wheeler registrations surged 2.45x and four-wheeler registrations doubled between FY18 and FY24, leading to higher CNG consumption, which makes up 60% of CGD volumes.
The number of CNG stations increased from 1,730 in 2019 to 7,444 by 9MFY25, facilitating greater CNG usage.
PNGRB's target of 126 million PNG-domestic connections by 2032 drives volume growth for piped natural gas to households.

pnl_drivers.description: EBITDA per standard cubic meter (SCM) is expected to moderate in FY25 due to lower APM allocation, with potential recovery from FY26 onwards, affecting profitability.

market_sizing.methodology: Forecasted Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR) for gas consumption volumes within the CGD sector for the period FY25-30, and revenue CAGR for key industry players for FY25-27.

demand_drivers.description: The need to connect more geographical areas and population to city gas networks drives significant capital investment.
Achieving projected gas consumption volumes requires substantial investment in pipeline infrastructure and distribution facilities.

pnl_drivers.description: Ongoing debt-funded capital expenditures may compress debt coverage metrics in the near term, influencing financial performance.

market_sizing.methodology: Estimated capital expenditure required for the CGD sector over a three-year period (FY25-27) to support its projected growth and expansion.
